questions.qtext:
Which of the following statements about Support Vector Machines (SVMs) is true?
S1 : SVMs can be used for both classification and regression tasks.
S2 : SVMs always require the use of Kernel functions to handle non-linearly separable data.
S3 : The hyperplane in SVM is chosen to maximize the margin between the classes.
S4 : The complexity of an SVM model is always linear in terms of the number of training samples.
Which of the following is/are correct?
questions.solution:
(c)
• SVMs can be used for classification (SVC) and regression (SVR) tasks. So, S1 is correct.
• Kernel functions are used when the data is not linearly separable, but SVMs can work withoutKernels if the data is linearly separable. So, S2 is incorrect.
• The SVM algorithm aims to find a hyperplane that maximizes the margin between the classes.
So, S3 is correct.
• The complexity of SVMs is quadratic with respect to the number of training samples, not linear. So, S4 is incorrect.

questions.qtext:
Consider the following statements:
S1 : The Bias-Variance Trade-Off helps in balancing the complexity of the model and its performance on unseen data.
S2 : A Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) can only approximate linear decision boundaries.
Which of the above is true?
questions.solution:
(a)
• The Bias-Variance Trade-Off helps balanced model complexity and performance on new data by managing error due to underfitting and overfitting. So, S1 is true.
• A Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) can approximate non-linear decision boundaries, no just linear ones. So, S2 is false.
questions.subject: Technical

questions.qtext:
Consider the following statements:
S1 : Decision Trees are prone to overfitting, especially when they are allowed to grow deep without pruning.
S2 : Cross-Validation provides an unbiased estimate of model performance by using multiple training and validation splits.
Which of the above is true?
questions.solution:
(c)
• Decision Trees can overfit the training data if they grow too deep without pruning. So, S1 is true.
• Cross-Validation provides an unbiased performance estimate by using splits of the data for training and validation. So, S2 is true.

questions.qtext: Which of the following statements is/are correct?

options.text: Linear regression assumes a linear relationship between the independent variables and the dependent variable.
In linear regression, the coefficient of determination R2 indicates the proportion of the variance in the dependent variable that is predictable from the independent variables.
The presence of multicollinearity in multiple linear regression increases the interpretability of individual predictors.
Ridge regression is used to reduce the bias in the estimated coefficients.

questions.solution:
(a, b)
• Linear regression assumes a linear relationship between the dependent variables. So, option (a) is correct.
• The coefficient of determination R2 indicates the proportion of the variance in the dependent variable that is explained by the independent variables. So, option (b) is correct.
• Multicollinearity decrease the interpretability of predicators by making it hard to isolate their individual effects. So, option (c) is incorrect.
• Ridge regression reduce variance and handles multicollinearity, which can introduce some bias but aims to stabilize the model, not reduce bias in coefficients. So, option (d) is incorrect.

questions.qtext: Which of the following statements is/are true?

options.text: In k-Nearest Neighbors (k-NN), the classification is based on the majority vote among the k nearest neighbors.
Lasso Regression includes all features in the final model, regardless of their relevance.
Principal Component Analysis (PCA) uses Euclidean distance to perform dimensionality reduction.
Logistic Regression estimates the probability of a binary outcome using a linear function.

questions.solution:
(a)
• k-NN classifies based on the majority vote among its k nearest neighbors. So, option (a) is correct.
• Lasso regression can set some coefficients to zero, effectively excluding less relevant features.
So, option (b) is incorrect.
• PCA performs dimensionality reduction using orthogonal transformations, not Euclidean distance. So, option (c) is incorrect.
• Logistic regression uses the logistic function (sigmoid) to estimate probabilities, not a linear function. So, option (d) is incorrect.
questions.subject: Technical

questions.qtext: Which of the following statements is/are true?

options.text: Lasso Regression is a method that does not perform feature selection.
The F1 Score is a measure of a model’s accuracy considering both precision and recall.
Gradient Boosting combines multiple models into a single model by averaging their predictions.
Logistic Regression is a technique used for regression tasks involving multiple classes.

questions.solution:
(b)
• The F1 Score is the harmonic mean of precision and recall. So, option (a) is correct.
• Lasso Regression performs feature selection by setting some coefficients to zero. So, option (b) is incorrect.
• Gradient Boosting builds models sequentially, correcting errors of previous models, not by averaging predictions. So, option (c) is incorrect.
• Logistic Regression is used for binary classification, not regression tasks. So, option (d) is incorrect.
questions.subject: Technical

questions.qtext: Which of the following statements is/are true?

options.text: In linear regression, the R-squared value indicates the proportion of variance explained by the model.
Decision trees use only mean squared error for regression problems.
Naive Bayes assumes that features are dependent given the class label.
Support Vector Machines (SVM) can handle non-linear decision boundaries using the Kernel trick.

questions.solution:
(a, d)
• The R-squared value indicates the proportion of variance in the dependent variable explained by the independent variables in linear regression. So, option (a) is correct.
• Decision trees can use various criteria like mean squared error for regression, but they are not limited to just that. So, option (b) is incorrect.
• Naive Bayes assumes that features are independent given the class label, not dependent. So, option (c) is incorrect.
• The Kernel trick enable SVM to handle non-linear data by mapping it to a higher dimensional space where a linear decision boundary can be applied. So, option (d) is correct.

questions.qtext:
Which Kernel function is commonly used with SVMs to handle non-linearly separable data?
I. Linear Kernel
II. Polynomial Kernel
III. Radial Basis Function (RBF) Kernel
IV. Sigmoid Kernel
questions.solution:
(c)
• The linear Kernel is used for linearly separable data. So, I is incorrect.
• The polynomial kernel can handle non-linearly separable data by transforming it into a higherdimensional space. So, II is correct.
• The RBF Kernel is also commonly used to handle non-linearly separable data by mapping it to a higher-dimensional space. So, III is correct.
• The sigmoid Kernel can also handle non-linearly separable data but is less commonly used compared to the polynomial and RBF Kernels. So, IV is correct.

questions.qtext: Which of the following statements is/are true?

options.text: The Mean Squared Error (MSE) penalizes larger errors more than smaller ones.
Lasso Regression decreases some coefficients to zero by penalizing squared values of the coefficient.
Logistic Regression uses the sum of squared coefficients for regularization.
k-Nearest Neighbors (k-NN) classifies based on random selection among its k nearest neighbors.

questions.solution:
(a)
• MSE penalizes larger errors more because it squares the errors. So, option (a) is correct.
• Lasso Regression (L1 regularization) penalizes absolute values, not squared values. So, option (b) is incorrect.
• Logistic Regression uses L1 or L2 regularization, not the sum of squared coefficients, which is associated with Ridge Regression. So, option (c) is incorrect.
• k-NN classifies based on the majority class among its k nearest neighbors, not random selection. So, option (d) is incorrect.

questions.qtext:
A k-nearest neighbors (k-NN) classifier is trained on a small dataset and achieves 100% accuracy by setting k = 1. Which of the following models trained on the same dataset is most likely to also achieve 100% accuracy?
(i) A decision tree with maximum depth equal to the number of training samples.
(ii) A linear support vector machine (SVM).
(iii) A logistic regression model.
(iv)A polynomial kernel SVM with degree 2.
questions.solution:
(a)
• A decision tree with a maximum depth equal to the number of training samples can perfectly fit the training data, achieving 100% accuracy.
• A linear SVM and logistic regression may not achieve 100% accuracy if the data is not linearly separable.
• A polynomial kernel SVM with degree 2 could achieve 100% accuracy if the data is polynomially separable, but it’s not guaranteed like the decision tree in this case.

questions.qtext: In a K-class dataset, you decide to use a Naïve Bayes classifier. The dataset contains N points, each described using D features, where each feature is categorical and can take V values. If you merge two of the K classes into a single class, how does this affect the number of parameters to estimate?

options.text: The number of parameters remains the same.
The number of parameters depends on D.

questions.solution:
(b)
If you merge two classes, the total number of classes K decreases by 1, which reduces the number of parameters that need to be estimated. Specifically, for the Naive Bayes classifier:
The number of class priors decreases from K to K – 1.
The number of conditional probabilities decreases from K × D × V to (K – 1) × D × V.

questions.qtext:
Consider the following statements:
S1 : The depth of a decision tree directly controls its bias and variance.
S2 : Decision trees are naturally resistant to overfitting.
S3 : Entropy in decision trees is a measure of randomness in the data.
S4 : In decision trees, features are chosen for splitting based on their correlation with the output variable.
Which of the above statements is correct?
questions.solution:
(c)
• The depth of a decision tree affects its bias-variance tradeoff. A deeper tree may lead to overfitting (low bias, high variance), while a shallower tree may lead to underfitting (high bias, low variance). So, S1 is correct.
• Decision trees are prone to overfitting, especially when they are deep and complex. So, S2 is incorrect.
• Entropy is used in decision trees to measure the uncertainty or randomness in a dataset. So, S3 is correct.
• Decision trees choose features based on criteria like Information Gain, not directly based on their correlation with the output variable. So, S4 is incorrect.
questions.subject: Technical

questions.qtext:
Which of the following statements about hierarchical clustering is/are correct?
S1 : Hierarchical clustering can be either agglomerative or divisive.
S2 : In agglomerative clustering, each point starts as its own cluster, and clusters are iteratively merged.
S3 : In divisive clustering, all points start in one cluster, and clusters are iteratively split.
S4 : Hierarchical clustering always results in a unique final clustering.
questions.solution:
(d)
• Hierarchical clustering can indeed be agglomerative or divisive. So, S1 is correct.
• Agglomerative clustering starts with each point as its own cluster and merges them iteratively.
So, S2 is correct.
• Divisive clustering starts with all points in one cluster and splits them iteratively. So, S3 is correct.
• Hierarchical clustering does not always result in a unique final clustering, as different linkage methods may yield different results. So, S4 is incorrect.
questions.subject: Technical

questions.qtext:
Which of the following statements about cross-validation methods is/are correct?
S1 : In k-fold cross-validation, the dataset is split into k equal parts, with each part being used as a validation set exactly once.
S2 : Leave-One-Out (LOO) cross-validation can be less biased than k-fold cross-validation.
S3 : k-fold cross-validation always results in a lower variance of performance estimates compared to LOO.
S4 : LOO cross-validation can be more prone to variance in performance estimates compared to k- fold cross-validation.
questions.solution:
(c)
• In k-fold cross-validation, each part is used as the validation set once. So, S1 is correct.
• LOO can be less biased because it uses nearly all data for training. So, S2 is correct.
• k-fold cross-validation does not always have lower variance; LOO can have lower variance.
So, S3 is incorrect.
• LOO can be more variable because each training set is slightly different. So, S4 is correct.

questions.qtext: Which of the following statements about Leave-One-Out (LOO) cross-validation is/are correct?

options.text: LOO is less prone to overfitting compared to k-fold cross-validation.
LOO can be very computationally expensive, especially for large datasets.
LOO uses each sample as a validation set exactly once, ensuring that the model is tested on all available data.
LOO can lead to high variance in performance estimates due to the small size of the training sets.

questions.solution:
(b, c, d)
• LOO can be more prone to overfitting because each training set is almost the same, and the model is validated on almost the entire dataset. So, option (a) is incorrect.
• LOO is computationally expensive since it requires training the model for each sample. So, option (b) is correct.
• LOO uses each sample as a validation set exactly once. So, option (c) is correct.
• LOO can lead to high variance in performance estimates because each training set is very similar to others, leading to potential overfitting So, option (d) is correct.
questions.subject: Technical

questions.qtext:
In the context of bias-variance trade-off:
(a) A model with high bias and high variance will have the lowest total error.
(b) Reducing model complexity usually decreases variance and increases bias.
(c) A model with low bias and low variance is ideal but often hard to achieve.
(d) Bias-variance trade-off is only relevant for linear models.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.solution:
(b, c)
• High bias and high variance do not result in the lowest total error; instead, it may result in high total error. So, option (a) is incorrect.
• Reducing model complexity generally decreases variance and increases bias. So, option (b) is correct.
• Achieving low bias and low variance is ideal but challenging. So, option (c) is correct.
• The bias-variance trade-off is relevant for all models, not just linear ones. So, option (d) is
incorrect.
